reading.body:
CyrusOne's Quincy facility (PNW1) publishes 36 megawatts of IT capacity. Assuming 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, this translates to roughly 900 racks. The campus occupies 720,000 square feet, which yields about 1.25 racks per thousand square feet, consistent with modern high-density AI infrastructure.

This facility ranks first among the two data centers in Washington state with published capacity specifications, and represents 60 percent of the state's total announced capacity of 60 megawatts. The state has 46 mapped data center facilities overall, the vast majority of which publish no power figure. The site is the largest published capacity facility in Washington by current records.

No certifications are published for this campus. The facility's location in Quincy places it in Grant County, in a region with access to hydroelectric power from the Columbia River system, though the campus's actual grid connection and power sourcing are not published.
